clue.text: One hat on husband following church party

indicators.note: following says the hat-and-husband group comes after the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England abbreviation

indicators.note: on, in an across clue, puts the hat before the husband

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Someone dons a hat beside her husband and heads off from church to a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceilidh is a Scottish or Irish social gathering with folk music and dancing, a kind of party.

clue.text: English politician on way to board at Heathrow?

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is the stock politician
a lane is a way or road

explanation.surface: An English MP heading off to catch a flight from Heathrow.
explanation.walkthrough: Heathrow is London's main airport, so boarding there means getting on an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: To emplane is to get on an aircraft, and boarding at an airport implies a plane.

clue.text: Maybe one's time to break for this

definitions.text: Maybe one's time to break for this

parts.words: Maybe one's time to break for this
parts.note: one o'clock is the classic hour to stop work for a midday meal, giving both a 'time' and a 'break' named after it

explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on the set phrases for the midday meal's time and the pause taken for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The midday meal is commonly taken around one o'clock, during a work break named after it.

clue.text: A bad, cruel criminal — be off, wicked nobleman!

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are crooked, bent out of their order
off tells us the letters of the word be leave the mixture before it is rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a cruel villain, telling the wicked aristocrat to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of A BAD CRUEL, with B and E from 'be' removed ('off'), are rearranged ('criminal').
explanation.definitionFit: Count Dracula, Bram Stoker's vampire, is an evil aristocrat of Transylvania.

clue.text: Distinguished women collecting silver they're awarded

indicators.note: collecting means the dames take the silver into their midst

parts.note: dames are women honoured with a title
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Honoured ladies gathering silverware as prizes are handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Damages are sums of money a court awards as compensation for loss or injury.

clue.text: Catch a cold in a public vehicle — you can count on it!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: catch tells the vehicle to take in what follows
in places the a-and-cold pair inside the vehicle

parts.note: a bus is a public transport vehicle
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Advice about picking up a chill on public transport, with a quip about reliability.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads for doing arithmetic, so it is literally a counting device.

clue.text: Macedonian general suffering from Oedipus complex?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., a general of Philip II and Alexander the Great
second meaning: split as ..., against the father (Latin pater), as Freud's Oedipus complex makes a son

explanation.walkthrough: Read the general's name as two parts: ANTI (against) and PATER (Latin for father).
explanation.definitionFit: Antipater was the regent of Macedon after Alexander's death, a celebrated general of antiquity.

clue.text: Worker in 16, genius at home becoming quiet

definitions.note: 16 is STONE, and Jacob Epstein was a sculptor who carved stone

indicators.note: becoming tells us the at-home letters turn into the quiet letter

parts.note: Albert Einstein is the byword for a genius
in means at home
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A stonemason who is clever at home falls silent.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 16 is STONE, the first half of 16/17.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Jacob Epstein was a twentieth-century sculptor famous for carving in stone.

clue.text: Appear in birthday suit and risk boredom?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: be naked, wearing no clothes
second meaning: have no engagements planned, so possibly be bored

explanation.walkthrough: A birthday suit is one's bare skin; the phrase also means having an empty diary.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both wearing no clothes and having no plans or appointments.

clue.text: Bridge partners at table drinking pop

indicators.note: drinking means the partners take the father inside them

parts.note: at the bridge table South and North are partners
pa and pop both mean father

explanation.surface: Card players at a bridge table sipping fizzy drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' looks like the card game but is the definition; the card game supplies the compass partners.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is the stretch of a bridge between supports, and to span is to bridge a gap.

clue.text: Gushing tap at basin for adult inducted in water ceremony?

indicators.note: gushing water pours out wildly, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tap gushing into a basin at a baptism for a grown-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabaptists hold that baptism should be given to believing adults, not infants, so their members are baptised as grown-ups.

clue.text: Breath-sweetener is something nutty, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the nut's name is to be taken as spoken

parts.note: a cashew is a nut

explanation.surface: Someone describes a breath mint as tasting of nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A cachou is a small scented lozenge sucked to freshen the breath.

clue.text: Finally some money secures protective gear — so workers are properly this?

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word some

parts.note: its final letter is E

indicators.note: secures means the money holds the gear inside it

parts.note: quid is British slang for a pound
PPE is personal protective equipment

explanation.surface: Spending money to buy safety kit so staff are properly kitted out.
explanation.walkthrough: A quid is a British pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers given protective gear are kitted out or furnished with what they need.

clue.text: Chief leader writer, fiery beast

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
a dragon is a fire-breathing beast

explanation.surface: A list of a top person, an author, and a fire-breathing monster.
explanation.definitionFit: Pendragon was the title of an ancient British supreme chieftain, as in Uther Pendragon.

clue.text: What could make adult shortly be led astray? Being this?

definitions.text: What could make adult shortly be led astray? Being this?

indicators.note: astray says the letters go off course into a new order
shortly cuts the word adult short, dropping its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A question about whether a gullible grown-up could be led astray.
explanation.walkthrough: ADUL (adult with its last letter dropped by 'shortly') plus BE LED, mixed ('astray'), gives the answer, and being easily misled is exactly what makes one led astray.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deludable can be fooled or misled, which is how an adult gets led astray.

clue.text: Hard barriers, old and new, within seats

indicators.note: within places the old-and-new letters inside the seats

parts.note: the stalls are the seats on the ground floor of a theatre
taken as written

explanation.surface: Walls ancient and modern around the seating in a venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Walls built of stone are solid, hard barriers, typical of field boundaries.

clue.text: See 16
A learner falling short — the first person to go under in this world?

indicators.note: to go under, in a down clue, places the first person below the rest
falling short means the trainee loses his last letter

parts.note: a cadet is a trainee, a learner in the forces
me is the first person pronoun

explanation.surface: A trainee failing the test, as someone is first to sink.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the academic world of universities and scholarship.

clue.text: Cook offering horse? Not English, bad!

indicators.note: not says the English letter is left out of the horse

parts.note: a charger is a cavalry horse
ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A chef serving horse meat, condemned as un-English and bad.
explanation.definitionFit: To chargrill is to cook food over intense heat on a grill so it is charred.

clue.text: News agency man needing extra time to speak again

indicators.note: needing extra means the agency man takes in one more letter

parts.note: Paul Julius Reuter founded the Reuters news agency

explanation.surface: A reporter has to ask for additional time to repeat himself.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-utter is to say something a second time, voicing it once more.

clue.text: The French fools — they're cut off and wet

parts.note: la is French for the (feminine)
goons are fools or idiots

explanation.surface: French fools getting soaked and stranded.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagoons are stretches of water separated from the sea by reefs or sandbanks.

clue.text: Shoddy stuff aboard ship piles up

indicators.note: aboard puts the goods on board, inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS is steamship
tack is cheap, tasteless goods, the root of tacky

explanation.surface: Cheap cargo heaped up on a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To stack is to pile things one on top of another.

clue.text: Unfinished book in which lad engages with computers etc

indicators.note: engages means the lad holds the other letters inside him

parts.note: a son is a boy
and can mean with, as in plus
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A boy absorbed in his computer leaves a book half read.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanditon is the novel Jane Austen left incomplete at her death in 1817.

clue.text: Sort of deficiency that brings back bitterness in European Union

indicators.note: brings back says the whole assembly reads from the end
in places the bitterness inside the union letters

parts.note: EU is the European Union
gall means bitterness, as in bile

explanation.surface: Resentment in Europe about a shortfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Ullage is the amount by which a container falls short of full, a particular shortfall.

clue.text: Voltaire exuding anger could become a sort of green

indicators.note: could become says what remains is turned into a different word
exuding means letting the anger seep out of the philosopher's name

parts.note: ire means anger

explanation.surface: The French writer losing his temper turns green.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove IRE from VOLTAIRE ('exuding'), leaving VOLTA, then rearrange it ('could become').
explanation.definitionFit: Lovat is a muted greyish-green colour, used chiefly of tweeds.

clue.text: Language of terrible boaster carrying zero credit

indicators.note: terrible means the boaster's letters are badly mangled

parts.note: O is the zero figure
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A dreadful braggart with no credit to his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Serbo-Croat is the South Slavic tongue spoken in Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Montenegro.

clue.text: Instrument, one featured in short book

indicators.note: featured in places the one inside the book

parts.note: vol is short for volume, a book
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A musical instrument shown in a slim volume.
explanation.definitionFit: The viol is a bowed stringed instrument of the Renaissance, ancestor of the viola da gamba family.

clue.text: Decline right away, leading to death

indicators.note: away says the right letter is taken out

parts.note: to decline is to decrease

explanation.surface: A sudden fall in health leading straight to someone dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Decease is a formal word for dying, the end of a life.

clue.text: Savage very dry? Just a bit

parts.note: brut describes champagne that is very dry
the suffix -ish means somewhat, just a bit

explanation.surface: A wine is described as fierce, very dry, only slightly so.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutish means coarse and cruel like a beast, which is to say savage.
